cues.text: Oh, hi Jen and Irene! You two are heading to class, aren't you?
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Hey Bill, yes, we are just walking there now. It's a little bit early now, though. We still would like to make some preparations for our apparatus for the experiment practice! How about walking with us, come on?
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Of course, it's really great to catch up! How's it going with your experiment? Have you already chosen the subject you're going to test yet?
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: To be honest, so far it is going well, and we're now serving as the laboratory partners responsible for conducting the test.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Also, we've decided to test the impacts of the gravitation force on a variety of objects with a number of densities.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Interesting indeed, but surely plenty of work for you to do. During the last two weeks, I've been thinking of and planning the test and eventually did it yesterday.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Goodness Irene, your hard work really left me with a deep impression.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Frankly, I'm into chemistry so much, so for me it's not very much like work. Whenever there is a little free time for me at the weekend, I'd like to spend it in the laboratory on my experiment, which almost feels like a second home to me.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: What about you, Bill? Which partner are you currently working with?
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Me and Kim, we were partnered by the tutor. I've never worked with him before, so I was worried at first that he wouldn't do that well in the lab work, but later it turns out he's so capable.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: I've noticed that he's always very well dressed.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Yeah, we share the same tastes in clothes; he's very stylish. But that doesn't keep him from getting hands dirty. He works very hard and makes significant contributions, which I really appreciate.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Ah, it's great that you and your partner get along with each other well, which I think will bring much more pleasure to your experiments when both of you work well together.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: What do you think of the other people in our group?
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Most boys are really good at math, which is really helpful when it comes to calculation.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Irene is also good at math, so she contributes a lot because she can do all the equations. I am mainly responsible for all the writing parts, since she finds it difficult. Without help between our partners, we'd probably fail.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: It can't be too true. And I'm so pleased that we've nearly completed it!
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Only because you finished the data analysis!
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Come on Jen, you give me too much credit!
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: I'm so happy that Linda has not been my partner again. In last experiment, Jen and I were grouped with her, which was really like a nightmare.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Yeah, though she always submitted her part of the group work on time, but she never took her phone with her, so it was unlikely for anyone to reach her and vice versa.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: We were quite annoyed at her attitude, but she was such a hard worker in all fairness, because she realised the amount of work that needed to get a high score.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Jen is so hard-working in fact; she has been invited to work on the professor's individual project.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Wow, really? That's amazing! Congrats! Do you know why he picked you?
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: I thought that was because I was closer to him, but he told me he was impressed by my always completing reading assignments in time for class.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: I bet you will be really popular between the other students when they find out. All of them want to hear about the project.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: You can distribute tasks to everyone, so all of them will get the chance to be part in it.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: It actually sounds quite good! Could you help me decide who to assign each task to?
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Sure! Now, let's see. Well, Irene finds writing difficult, but that might be a good opportunity for her to practice it by reviewing the bibliography?
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Bibliography, I think, may be a bit too long for me, so the methodology shall be a better choice.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Sure, that makes sense. Bill, you said that Kate is a hard-working girl. So I think she could be given the conclusion part, as it requires plenty of effort.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Ok, sure. And I know that Kyle hasn't been feeling well recently, so she could be tasked with the abstract and the acknowledgement for there is very little work involved.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: Jen, would you like to do the literature review part? Basically, there is a lot of work to do but I believe you really enjoy writing, so I think you'll do a good job.
cues.speaker: Irene

cues.text: Sure, sounds great.
cues.speaker: Jen

cues.text: Right, so now bibliography and the discussion are left to assign. I think Linda will be struggling with the referencing, considering the amount of work.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: So perhaps, I will take care of that task and she could do bibliography.
cues.speaker: Bill

cues.text: That's great, guys. Thanks for your help! I'll tell the tutor when he arrives.
cues.speaker: Irene
